correctness.rationale: For 0<α≤1, 0<θ≤1, the differentiated distortion is a product of two series with nonnegative coefficients. For 1<θ≤2/(1+α), 0<α<1, the exact ODE yields (n+1)a[n+1]=[A+(1-s)n]a[n]+s(n+1)a[n-1], with A≥0 and 0<s<1, proving positivity at all indices by induction. T(1)=1 normalizes the resulting integer-valued weights and its Laplace transform ψ is completely monotone, hence valid in every finite dimension. For α>1 the second generator derivative is negative near t=0. For 0<α≤1 and θ above the bound, the negative second e^{-t} coefficient contradicts positivity of any Laplace measure, after showing its support starts at 1. Every normalization, parameter endpoint and quantifier was checked. The bundled standard-library checker independently matches 9 exact rational expansions and tests the boundary; finite checks are only supplementary.

originality.rationale: The 2024 originating full text defines the same distortion but treats bivariate copulas, gives a sufficient convexity rectangle only, and names higher dimensions as future work. The new result goes beyond the elementary extension of that convexity range by proving complete monotonicity for all derivatives in the new parameter strip with a positive integer-valued frailty law. The 2020 work with an almost identical title has a different distortion. The 2009 all-dimensional general criterion and known Joe/AMH one-parameter subfamilies are explicitly separated from this family-specific result. No published research-record hit or inspected primary source was found to imply the full claim; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Unindexed or inaccessible work may contain an equivalent all-dimensional criterion or identify the same positive-integer mixture.

The sharp convexity boundary alone is implicit in a known second-derivative formula, so the genuine contribution is specifically the all-dimensional complete-monotonicity equivalence and explicit frailty recurrence.
No independent audit or comprehensive human literature survey has been performed.

value.rationale: The 2024 model was introduced and studied only in two dimensions, while its conclusion specifically notes the challenges of multivariate distortions. The result determines exactly when the canonical family can model arbitrary finite-dimensional dependence and gives a practical latent integer-frailty representation. The nonempty θ>1 extension for α<1 goes beyond the published sufficient rectangle and is not a routine application of convexity: proving all dimensions requires an all-order coefficient positivity argument. The theorem also distinguishes all-dimensional admissibility from bivariate validity on the AMH boundary. This is a motivated complete structural classification, not merely a numerical refinement.
